title: cyclobalanopsis kerrii

It is native to Southeast Asia, particularly in the mountainous regions of China, Thailand, and Myanmar. The Kerri's chestnut oak is valued for its medicinal properties, which include potential health benefits such as anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial effects. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which are responsible for its therapeutic actions, including anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects.
